newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA WANTS GREATER MARKET ACCESS IN SOUTH ASIA.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA WANTS GREATER MARKET ACCESS IN SOUTH ASIA.

text.p: Sri Lanka is lobbying for greater market access for its products in neighbouring India and Pakistan, the state-owned Daily News said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said Sri Lankan trade officials had stressed the need for tariff reduction and the removal of non-tariff barriers, an impediment to market access, with their Indian and Pakistani counterparts at a recent meeting.
The inter-government group on trade liberalisation of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) met in the Nepalese capital of Kathmandu two weeks ago, the newspaper said.
It said Sri Lanka also wants transparency in information on subsidies to be given by SAARC nations to their exports and domestic industries.

Sri Lanka proposed that under the rule of origin, the import content of its products should be increased to 60-70 percent from the current less-than-50 percent, as its exporters relied to a great extent on imported inputs to their products, the newspaper said.
Sri Lanka's exports to SAARC members in 1996 were worth six billion rupees, or 2.6 percent of its total exports. Imports from the region were worth 36.3 million, or 12.1 percent of total imports.
In 1995, the respective percentages were 2.6 percent and 10.2 percent.
The 12-year-old SAARC groups India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, the Maldives and Sri Lanka.
SAARC was formed to improve the economies of the South Asian nations, which together hold more than one fifth of the world's population.
